findings.claim: Two of the six meta files declare themselves `[DEEP]` while the pipeline key file's Meta Documents table records them as `[PARTIAL]`. Both statements are current, neither carries a marker acknowledging the other, and they cannot both hold. Status is the signal downstream stages use to decide whether a meta document is finished, so the two readings produce different behaviour: `[DEEP]` means consume it, `[PARTIAL]` means it still needs deepening before /create-prd.

findings.claim: The Release Plan's one-line definition of v1 says split capture happens 'at source' — a term this tree defines as rung 2, inside the DAW, explicitly NOT v1 and NOT authorised. The table row six lines below states the opposite for the same release. D-70 exists precisely to purge this wording, and the tree treats an overclaim as an unrecoverable trust breach, so the residue is not cosmetic: it is the exact sentence a positioning or planning reader lifts as the v1 objective.

findings.forcedInvention: How many of the 101 boundary problems are resolved by Section-1 mechanism extraction — 65 or 85 — and what happened to the ~16 that no class accounts for. The verdict paragraph and the classification table give different answers for the same quantity, and a reader scoping the extraction work for /create-prd must pick one without any source to pick it from.
findings.claim: Section 3 states that 101 boundary problems 'were classified into' four classes, then gives class counts that sum to ~85, leaving ~16 of the stated pool unclassified; and the verdict paragraph attributes '~85 of the 101' to the mechanism-extraction class that the table itself sizes at ~65. The ~85 figure is the sum of all four classes, so the verdict conflates 'total classified' with 'the extraction class' — two statements about the same quantity that cannot both hold, with no marker on either.
findings.evidence: .memory/wiki/specs/ideation/meta/cross-cut-emergent-capabilities.md:5 — 'Source pool: 83 candidate emergent cross-cuts (`emCC`), 90 candidate emergent features (`emF`), 101 boundary problems (`bp`).'  ·  :227-229 — 'The 101 boundary problems were classified into: (a) **clean/defended seams**...; (b) **tooling mis-tags**...; (c) **unowned coordination seams / gaps**...; (d) **genuine merge / shared-owner candidates**.'  ·  :239-240 — '**The fix for ~85 of the 101 is mechanism extraction per Section 1 — not domain merger.**'  ·  CONTRADICTED BY the class table at :250-253 — '| Clean / defended seams (evidence FOR split) | ~10 | ... |', '| Tooling mis-tags (not real seams) | 2 | ... |', '| Unowned coordination seams / cross-cut mis-modelled as feature | ~65 | ... | **Extract Section-1 mechanism** |', '| Genuine merge / shared-owner candidates | ~8 | ... |'. 10 + 2 + 65 + 8 = 85 ≠ 101.

findings.claim: The Budget axis is declared with a posture but explicitly no value, and the decision rule it supplies is untestable in the one case that matters. 'Prefer usage-based where a usage-based equivalent exists' decides the easy cases; the rule for the hard case — a capability with no cheaper equivalent — is that it 'must be justified', with no threshold to justify against. Two implementers pricing the same hosted-search or transcode decision reach opposite conclusions and both comply with the text.

findings.claim: Every success metric in the unit is directional. Each 'Measurable:' clause names a direction of travel with no number, no unit and no timeframe, so none is falsifiable and none can be tested at launch. This is the rubric's ⚠ condition verbatim ('Directional only') and it is uniform across all four personas and both counterparty profiles — there is no counter-example in the unit.
